title: Towards Full Participation of Persons with Disabilities in Singapore Society
what_it_is: Towards Full Participation of Persons with Disabilities in Singapore Society

sections.label: Estimated number of PwDs
sections.summary: NCSS estimated about a quarter million PwDs in Singapore in 2018, with over a million persons and families directly impacted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The National Council of Social Service or NCSS estimated in 2018 about 11,000 PwDs aged seven to 18 years, another 61,000 PwDs aged 19 to 49 years, and almost 200,000 PwDs aged 50 years and above.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This is about a quarter million people with disabilities in Singapore in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Add an average of three immediate family members to each PWD, and there are more than a million persons and families directly impacted by disability in Singapore.

sections.label: Public willingness to share
sections.summary: Sixty-four percent of the public polled were willing to share but not interact with PwDs in public spaces.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Sixty-four percent of the public polled were willing to share but not interact with PwDs in public spaces.

sections.label: PwD employment rate and options
sections.summary: The employment rate of PwDs is substantially lower than typical peers, and they face a limited range of work options.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The employment rate of PwDs is not only substantially lower than their typical peers, they face a limited range of work options.

sections.label: Areas where basics fall short
sections.summary: Seeing PwDs as part of Singapore society, areas where basics fall short must be scanned, including healthcare, accessibility, education and others.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Stemming from a perspective that PwDs are part and parcel of our Singapore society, then we need to get down to work and scan through carefully areas where the basics fall short – in healthcare, accessibility, education and especially lifelong learning, public communications, security and safety, housing, transport, jobs and economic security.

sections.label: Co-develop lifelong learning solution
sections.summary: In learning, co-develop a bolder lifelong learning solution with PwDs, disability organisations and industry captains, with vision, strategies, outcomes and reporting.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In learning, co-develop a bolder lifelong learning solution with PwDs, disability organisations, key industry captains, complete with vision, strategies, outcomes, tracking and reporting mechanism.

sections.label: Public reporting of Enabling Masterplan
sections.summary: Many are unaware of Enabling Masterplan progress, so there ought to be commitment to public reporting of deliverables, progress, outcomes and challenges.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Many people are not aware of the progress of the Enabling Masterplan even if good work is being driven, being done.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: There ought to be a commitment to public reporting of key agreed deliverables, progress, outcomes, challenges and even calls for participation and for help.

sections.label: Government alliance with disability community
sections.summary: The speaker proposes a formal, ongoing alliance with PwDs, families and disability organisations for co-visioning, key decisions and future planning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In a vision that needs the support of the whole of society, Government's engagement and collaboration with PwDs, their families, disability organisations must be central.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, I propose a more formal and on-going alliance of sorts where co-visioning, key decisions, future planning are made; so that decisions are not made in silos, depending on which Government agency or Ministry gets the most budget, so that we can avoid the damaging "cliff effects" when one Ministry's work passes on to the next, so that resources can be allocated from a "life-cycle" perspective, knowing that each move made will impact the rest of the whole eco-system.

sections.label: Clarifying Many-Helping-Hands roles
sections.summary: Roles and responsibilities of the Many-Helping-Hands must be clarified and updated based on a common desired end and each helper's strengths.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Clarification of roles and responsibilities of the "Many-Helping-Hands" has to be made, updated, based on a common desired end in mind and the strengths and attributes of each helping hand.

sections.label: Developing disability community leaders
sections.summary: The speaker calls for developing leaders in the disability community and including the voice of PwDs and their proxies in policy-making and implementation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We should therefore develop as many leaders as we can identify in the disability community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: And we must listen and include the voice of PwDs and their proxies in policy-making and implementation.

sections.label: Supporting PwDs full participation
sections.summary: Noting some are born with disabilities and some become disabled with age, the speaker urges the House and Singapore to support PwDs' full participation and dignified lives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Some of us are born with disabilities and some of us will become disabled with age.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I urge this House and the rest of Singapore to support this call to ensure that all PwDs can fully participate in our society and they can all lead dignified and meaningful lives in our society.

sections.label: Compulsory Education Act amendment
sections.summary: The Compulsory Education Act was amended to include students with moderate to severe special educational needs, signalling an education system for all students.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Another milestone was the amendment of the Compulsory Education Act to include students with moderate to severe special educational needs, which sends a strong signal that our education system is for all students.

sections.label: Sports participation rates among PwDs
sections.summary: Surveys show sports participation rates among PwDs almost doubled from 28% in 2015 to 51% in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Surveys show that sports participation rates among PwDs have almost doubled from 28% in 2015 to 51% in 2018.

sections.label: Enabling Employment Credit for disabled
sections.summary: The new Enabling Employment Credit will replace existing wage offsets expiring in December 2020 for employers of Singaporeans with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The new Enabling Employment Credit will replace existing wage offsets that expire in December 2020, for employers of Singaporeans with disabilities.

sections.label: Wage support for disabled hires
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Heng announced the Government will give 50% wage support under the Jobs Growth Incentive to new local PwDs hired by firms increasing local headcount.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng announced last week that the Government will provide the higher tier of wage support of 50% under the Jobs Growth Incentive to all new local PwDs hired by firms that increase their local headcount.

sections.label: Support for families of disabled
sections.summary: CareShield Life was introduced for severe disability, and the Home Care-giving Grant gives monthly cash pay-outs to eligible individuals with permanent moderate disability.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: To better support families caring for persons with moderate to severe disability, we recently introduced CareShield Life for those with severe disability.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The Home Care-giving Grant also provides monthly cash pay-outs to offset care-giving costs for eligible individuals with permanent moderate disability.

sections.label: SNTC trust accounts growth
sections.summary: The number of SNTC trust accounts has grown almost 10 times over the last decade, to over 795 accounts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The number of SNTC trust accounts has grown by almost 10 times over the last decade, to over 795 accounts.

sections.label: Third Enabling Masterplan workgroups contributions
sections.summary: Over 200 PwDs, care-givers and sector partners contributed ideas last year to three thematic cross-sectoral workgroups under the Third Enabling Masterplan.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Last year, over 200 PwDs, care-givers and sector partners contributed ideas to three thematic cross-sectoral workgroups launched under the Third Enabling Masterplan, on the topics of inclusion within preschools, employment and independent living respectively.
